children.value: This notebook covers some of the basics of using Pandas.
It is meant to get you acquainted with how Pandas does some common data operations, not to provide in depth coverage of the library.
Basic operations include filtering and selecting data from an existing dataset.
In this notebook, We will use the
dataset, which contains every flight that departed from a New York City airport in 2013. The data comes from the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Actual departure and arrival times (Format: Local time, HHMM or HMM). Missing values (NA) represent canceled flights.
Scheduled departure and arrival times (Format: Local time, HHMM or HMM).
Departure and arrival delays, measured in minutes. Negative times represent early departures/arrivals.
Two-letter airline carrier abbreviation (maps to the airlines table).
Aircraft tail number (maps to the planes table). Missing values (NA) represent canceled flights.
Origin airport code (EWR, JFK, or LGA; maps to airports and weather).
Amount of time spent in the air, measured in minutes.
Distance between origin and destination airports, measured in miles.
Scheduled departure time broken down into hour and minute components.
Scheduled date and time of the flight formatted as a timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Used for joining directly with the weather table.

If you are currently writing code, let me know if you need help with a specific programming language (like R or Python) or a particular data manipulation query (such as calculating average delays by carrier).

Are there any redundant columns? These are columns that repeat data in other columns.
Are there any analytical columns? These are columns that are computed from one or more other columns.
